items.root_cause: test-guards.ps1's restore model covers what the HARNESS writes and nothing the SUBJECT writes. A guard that persists a high-water mark is a stateful subject: driven over a deliberately shrunken board it LEARNS the shrunken count (33 -> 24) as its new floor, and restoring the board does not restore what it learned, so every later guards run - including the final one with no mutation at all - is measured against a mark the harness taught it. The same family has bitten this file twice before at the mtime layer (a restore that left product-urls.json newer than name-drift.json held tile-integrity for every later case: FreezeMtime, 2026-08-30; case 14's name-drift rerun) and each was patched inside one case; the general mechanism - subject state that persists between child runs is never put back - was never addressed, and a new ratchet (09-05) reached it on the first run.

root_fix.what: make the harness restore GUARD STATE after every child run, discovered by shape rather than listed by name, and prove it with a frozen fixture - without touching any ratchet, guard or baseline
root_fix.exact_change: (1) Immediately after the 'baseline: guards pass' case (line 396), register every file matching out/*-baseline.json with Backup() (6 files today, 5,034 bytes; the glob, never a hand list, so the next ratchet is covered on the day it lands; note _baseline.json / _baseline-batch.json do NOT match, on purpose - they are multi-MB verify-no-regression snapshots). (2) A helper RestoreGuardState that calls RestoreNow (bytes + mtime) on each registered baseline path, invoked after the child returns in RunGuardsOut (after line 225), CheckLoud (after 300), CheckScript (after 313), CheckWarn (after 684) and the direct ad-line run (after 632) - five call sites, one helper. (3) Before the residue tripwire (1014), a 'ratchet hygiene' tripwire: for each registered baseline, compare bytes to the pre-run snapshot; print PASS 'no ratchet learned from a mutated board' or FAIL naming the file and its before/after counts; count it in $pass/$failed like every other case. (4) test-guards.ps1 -SelfTest (the existing block at 150-185) gains frozen cases: a temp out/ with a 219-byte cells=33 baseline, a simulated child that overwrites it with cells=24 and a fresh mtime, then RestoreGuardState -> bytes AND mtime identical (MUST RESTORE); the same overwrite with RestoreGuardState skipped -> the hygiene tripwire names it (MUST FIRE); an untouched baseline -> the restore is a no-op write and the tripwire is silent (MUST NOT FIRE). Do NOT add a learn-suppressing switch to audit-band-censorship, audit-json-readers or audit-board-mojibake, and do NOT pass anything new through guards.ps1: a disarm path in production code leaks (an env or switch set in a session that then runs the daily chain stops the ratchet tightening silently - the rules-that-silently-disarm shape), and it would have to be threaded to every current and future kid, a hand-maintained registry of the kind item dc7460 is about. (5) OPTIONAL, for the fifth-failure class (cause unproven, see evidence): in case 8c, before mutating, Skip with 'tile-integrity is HELD at baseline: out/name-drift.json is older than product-urls.json in this copy - re-run audit-name-drift before the suite' when name-drift.json's LastWriteTimeUtc is earlier than product-urls.json's, so an inherited stale mtime reads as the precondition failure it is rather than as a broken invariant. Bringing the baseline under Backup() ALONE is also insufficient: RestoreAll runs once at the end, and the failures are mid-run - the restore has to follow every child.

items.resolution_note: Bounce premise HOLDS: test-guards case 18 halves Walmart's cells, audit-band-censorship counts 24 censored cells instead of 33 and TIGHTENS its baseline to 24 inside the hermetic copy, the board is restored and the baseline is not, and every later guards run - four expect-0 cases including the final 'restored' one - fails on a ratchet nobody touched. Reproduced in a 3-command scratch replica and in a full hermetic run. Class: the harness restores what it wrote, never what the guard under test wrote; a ratchet is a stateful subject. Fixed in the harness only: every out/*-baseline.json is snapshotted and put back (bytes + mtime) after every child run, a hygiene tripwire names any ratchet that learned during the suite, and frozen self-test cases prove both. No ratchet was weakened and no baseline was edited.

The glob was measured, not assumed: grocery/out/*-baseline.json matches 6 of the 9 files whose name contains 'baseline', totalling 5,034 bytes, and correctly excludes _baseline.json, _baseline-batch.json and _baseline-rye.json. items.deviation: THREE deviations, all inside the plan's own intent. (1) RegisterGuardState is called just INSIDE the try block rather than between the 'baseline: guards pass' line and it, so a throw during registration still unwinds through RestoreAll. Same instant in the run, strictly safer. (2) root_fix (5), the OPTIONAL fifth-failure hardening, was implemented against BOTH of audit-tile-integrity's staleness dependencies, not just product-urls.json: its own lines 69-89 hold when out/name-drift.json is older than product-urls.json OR the newest comparison, and naming only the first would let a comparison-driven hold arrive wearing case 8c's name. Case 8c now Skips with the precondition named. THE FIFTH FAILURE IS STILL NOT REPRODUCED AND IS NOT CLAIMED AS FIXED: live mtimes at implementation were out/name-drift.json 11:47:13 and product-urls.json 11:29:20, so tile-integrity is NOT held on this tree and the new Skip does not fire; it exists so that an inherited stale mtime reads as a rotted precondition instead of a broken invariant. (3) The hygiene tripwire also reports a baseline that APPEARED during the suite (a ratchet landing mid-run writes its first high-water mark from a mutated board and no snapshot exists to put it back). That branch is covered by its own must-fire case rather than shipping untested. MUTATION-PROVEN, four ways, each on a scratch copy and never on the live file: disarming RestoreGuardState -> MUST RESTORE fails; blinding the LEARNED comparison -> MUST FIRE fails; widening the restore to every registered file -> CLEAN TWIN fails; dropping the mtime half of RestoreNow -> MUST RESTORE fails. Each mutation produced exactly its own failure and no other. PARKED, NOT BOUNCED, AND NOT MINE - the fix worked and revealed a second defect standing behind the first. run-test-guards-weekly.ps1 after the fix (13:50:30 to 14:16:33) is 'negative tests: 32 passed, 2 failed', EXIT 1, and the plan required 0. Before the fix the reviewer measured 29 passed / 4 failed / rc 1 with all four failures reading 'expected exit 0, got 2' and every one of them carrying the band-censorship RATCHET line as its evidence. After the fix NO failure mentions the ratchet at all: 'PASS ratchet hygiene: 0 of 6 guard baseline(s) learned from a mutated board', 'PASS residue tripwire', 'PASS coverage regression: Walmart loses half its priced cells between boards (exit 2)' (case 18, the tightening case, unchanged), and both 'PASS delegate stderr: a benign diagnostic line ... must not crash the gate (exit 0)' and 'PASS restored: guards pass again after every mutation is reverted (exit 0)' - two of the four founding failures now pass. The remaining two are the board-vs-identity pair, and their FAILURE MODE CHANGED: they now get the exit code they expect (0) and fail the SIGNATURE check, 'exit 0 as expected BUT its own text is absent - this case proved nothing', with the cause printed right there in FailEvidence: 'board-vs-identity [staple]: BLIND - no identity rows at the current rules_hash b487e24c2e61 ... Nothing was compared, so nothing is proven; this is not agreement.' THAT CONDITION IS LIVE AND PRE-EXISTING, verified on the live tree at 14:20 and not in a copy: grocery/guards.ps1 exits 0, 'GUARDS OK: every hard invariant holds. Safe to publish', GUARDS-COMPLETE hard=0 warn=20, with band-censorship ok against the ratchet AND both board-vs-identity lanes reporting the same BLIND as warns. The cause is measurable and is not this change: the whole identity table carries exactly ONE rules_hash, ccf5c21e891e over 42,730 staple rows, written 2026-09-07 08:10:35-37 by the 08:00 chain, while commodities.json was edited at 11:10:36 (round 1's commit eb852a720) and the 11:28:28 rebuild did not re-emit identity. So the hash moved at 11:10 and the table has been stale against it since, hours before this session started at 13:40. It was invisible to the reviewer's own run because Check() tests the exit code before the signature, and the broken ratchet made every one of these cases exit 2 first - the ratchet fix is precisely what stopped the harness lying about which guard was broken. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY: re-emitting identity means running compare-deals, which is a board rebuild, and this round is explicitly forbidden from rebuilding or republishing the board; the gate ships ADVISORY so nothing is blocked; and tomorrow's 08:00 chain re-emits at the then-current hash and clears it. No case, expectation, threshold or fixture was relaxed to make the number look better. The harness already names the cause in its own failure evidence, so no further change was invented for it.

items.deviation: TWO refinements inside the plan's intent, both narrowing the fold so it cannot swallow an unrelated failure. (1) Only the DAILY run's non-zero RUN RECORD is demoted; the 07:00 ad run completes before check-ad-cycles ever runs guards, so its exit code can never be a symptom of the hold. (2) The FAILED line is demoted only for a task whose LastRunTime is at or before the verdict's `written` time; a task that started AFTER the refusal and failed is a separate failure and keeps its own top-level line. The fold itself was extracted into a pure Merge-HeldFindings so the -SelfTest drives the REAL assembly rather than the predicate alone - a fold tested only through its predicate proves nothing about the list the reader receives, which is where the cost lives. evidence: grocery/alert-log.txt 12:31:33: SENT 'Your call: the memory store's private backup remote, or a reviewed-exception path in the security guard' -> schweino68@gmail.com (id 1a07cecd8042c1bc); no script in the repo carries that subject (git grep), so it was an ad hoc send-alert.ps1 call by round 1's developer for item 4f672e (queue notes on 4f672e: 'BRAD'S CALL, emailed 2026-09-07'). send-alert.ps1:217-334 writes EVERY alert to triage-queue.json before mailing, derives the type key from the subject ('your call the memory store s private backup remote ...' vs 4f672e's 'ops the agent memory store has a finding'), and Get-QueueAction (85-110) never absorbs into a needs-brad item anyway (line 90), so the escalation minted a NEW open item at 12:31:31 with status 'open'. triage-close.ps1's disposition vocabulary (confirmed|false-alarm|superseded|by-design|wont-fix) has no way to park an item, so 4f672e's needs-brad status is a hand edit - the queue's readme says hand edits are for forcing a re-triage.
items.root_cause: the escalation path has no representation in the queue: send-alert can only give an item one status at birth (open) and the closer has no park disposition, so every needs-brad email re-enters the queue as fresh triage work, and each parked question costs one new open item per escalation - the estate's own 'an alert with no repair lane' shape pointed at its escalation lane.

root_fix.what: let an escalation be born parked: send-alert.ps1 -Escalates <queue-id> writes the new item with status needs-brad and notes 'escalation email for <id>' (the mail still goes out; the once-a-day gate and -Force are unchanged), so triage-due never lists it and the parked item stays the single owner of the question
root_fix.exact_change: param [string]$Escalates = ''; in the 'default' (new item) branch at 294-300 set status = if ($Escalates) { 'needs-brad' } else { 'open' } and notes = if ($Escalates) { 'escalation email for ' + $Escalates + ' (parked there; do not re-triage)' } else { $null }; in -SelfTest add the routing case. Blast radius (measured by reading the four consumers): triage-due.ps1:162/169 already lists only status open and counts needs-brad as parked; audit-alert-precision.ps1 judges only status resolved (62-76), so a parked-at-birth item is neither counted nor flagged; Get-QueueAction is unchanged (a needs-brad item never absorbs, so a second escalation for the same id mints a second parked item - bounded, manual, and visible in triage-due's parked count); validate-triage-plan is unaffected. No board, feed or page is touched.
